Running head and page number at the top.; One block of running text in one column, in the upper part of the scan; the lower part is blank. No margin notes. Signature mark at the foot of the text.

main_text.p: non possumus, neque omnibus simul objectisventipi-ctuariam realibus frui; estque necesse ut modò ex facultatibus unam ad objectum hoc applicemus, modò aliam ad aliud tunc absens,& umbra-tilem, quae idque ordine & modis debitis; non posset sane pro libertate nostra, neque ordinatimest Ratio, & facile ista facultas & objectorum commutatio sive successio fieri, nisi facultatemeruditionis superficia-ria fundamentum & quandam novi generis haberet Mens, quaecausa; uti ejusdem objecta absentia, eaque simul multa, ei depingeret, ut ex illa pictura substitutione,ideæ atque rationinia, illius sunt objectorum realium vices agente, memormateria & instrumen-tum. esset sese ad realia objecta absentia, sed repraesentata, convertendi; & de illis simul repraesentatis in mente, idealiter disponendi, quae postea facultatum realium objectis veris communicatione exsequeretur. Haec facultas depingendi nobis in mente objecta, quando tamen eorum realis praesentia a suis cuique propriis facultatibus abest, ea est quae Ratio humana sive intellectus a- ctibus dicitur, feque extendit ad pingenda quaevis tum spiritualia, tum corporea, Deum videlicet, ejus attributa, resque creatas cæteras, quarum picturæ vel icones ideæ jam vulgo dicuntur, harumque idearum complexus, comparatio, separatio, aliarum idearum ex prioribus deductio, ratiocinia vel ratiocinationes appellantur. Horum primum, Ratio videlicet, cùm sit eruditionis superficiariæ efficiens causa, idea vero ejus materia; ratiocinatio autem ejusdem tum ampliandi tum communicandi instrumentum; eorum proprietates affectionesve non sunt.

page.notes: Marginal notes in the right margin are small italic type; their exact word breaks are partly uncertain, notably the opening "ventipi-ctuariam" and "umbra-tilem", which may be misread. Their placement beside the lines is approximate. The first word is cut at the left edge and is read as "ctibus" with a [?] for the first letter, since the lead-in is mostly lost; the line-end of the running text is partly faded. The signature "E 5" is printed mid-line, and the catchword-like "sunt" at the right is taken as the line's end word, not a catchword. Some words in the last line are faint.
